note: PathPlanner2D's public routing surface, read back from the reference. Cases are tagged agreement/divergence: the route cache key is a deliberate change, so the reference is recorded as evidence of what was changed, not as the target.

nearest_free_point.note: exactly on the corner, margin applied
vegetation does not block, so unchanged
escape lies outside bounds; clamp fights push
clearance below the 0.5 m push floor
nested rings at a sub-floor clearance

plan_route.note: start on the boundary with a free way out
start exactly on the bounds margin
goal exactly on the bounds margin

route_waypoints.note: closed loop, nothing in the way
an anchor starts inside an obstacle
segments that cannot be routed are skipped
closed: the closing segment must detour
open: the same anchors never traverse the closing edge

cache_sequence.note: The reference's cache behaviour, which the port reproduces for a FIXED scene. What the port adds is a revision in the key, so a scene change misses instead of serving a route planned around obstacles that have moved -- the reference cannot express that, so there is nothing to record for it.

calls.note: 3 m away: snaps to the same key, hit
40 m away: a different key, miss
back to the first key, still hit
A again: hit, moves A to the end -> [B, A]
A: still cached because the hit saved it
+6: a different key under rounding, +5's under floor
0.4 m away: the 1.0 floor makes this the same key
